newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FORECAST-Portugal inflation seen easing November.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Portugal inflation seen easing November.

text.p: Portugal's inflation, as measured by the benchmark rolling 12-month average, looks set to have eased in November to 3.1 percent from 3.2 percent in October, analysts said.

Analyst forecasts for the month-on-month change in November ranged from a fall of 0.2 percent, due to a sharp decline in non-beef meat prices, to an increase of 0.1 percent, compared with a fall of 0.1 percent in October.
The rolling average would ease to 3.1 percent on any of these hypotheses, analysts said.
The year-on-year rate would be between 2.7 and 3.0 percent, against 3.0 percent in October.
The National Statistics Institute (INE) has still to announce the date for the release of the November inflation figures.
In November 1995, the month-on-month rise was 0.1 percent, with the average rate standing at 4.2 percent and the year-on-year 3.9 percent.
Analysts said the impact of fears over madcow disease on meat prices, which boosted the inflation rate earlier in the year, had been worked out of the index by November.
